Subject: PoC: GPU tiling & precision constraints

Hi Mina / Marcus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. We're ready to move the PoC forward but need a firm answer on two things before we lock the scope:

1) Our primary model will run with ~65k token windows (mix of long context + conversation history). We plan to maintain a KV cache for active sessions — roughly 300–600 concurrent sessions for the PoC.
2) We want to evaluate both 8-bit and 4-bit quantized variants; quality regressions are acceptable up to a small delta but we need to understand the resulting GPU footprint and whether you can support tiling (spanning context across multiple GPUs) or if we need a single-GPU 80GB-class solution.

Can you provide a short sizing estimate with assumptions (tokens per session, KV cache per token, batch concurrency), and note any operational limitations (prefetching, KV eviction, fallback behavior) we should expect?

Attaching a brief requirements sheet.

Cheers,

Subject: Re: PoC: GPU tiling & precision constraints

Hi Ari — thanks for the clear brief and the spec sheet. Quick reply with our initial back-of-envelope sizing and a couple of follow-ups.

Assumptions used here (call out):
- Model: gino-7B-xl (decoder-only style; KV per token ~ 1.1x model_dim bytes after compression in KV layout)
- Target window: 65,536 tokens active per session; average active tokens (working set) per session: 28k (because long tails are cold)
- Concurrent sessions: 450 (mid of your 300–600 range)
- Batch concurrency: we assume 60 concurrent requests at peak; average request length 256 tokens

Prelim sizing (single-request working memory + KV):
- Unquantized FP16 peak working set per sequence on a single GPU: ~18–22 GB (includes activations + temporary buffers)
- KV cache (FP16) for 28k active tokens per session: ~28k * 1.1 * 8 bytes ≈ 246KB/session → for 450 sessions ≈ 108 GB total (this dominates)

Quantization effects (rough guide):
- FP16 -> int8 (dynamic mixed-precision kernels): KV storage drops ~50–60% depending on packing (so 108 GB → ~48–54 GB). Compute working-set reductions smaller (~20–30%) as activations still need higher precision paths.
- FP16 -> 4-bit (grouped quantization / Q4xx): KV storage can drop ~65–75% (108 GB → ~27–38 GB). Note: some runtimes use 8-bit for KV and 4-bit for weights — results vary.

Tiling / multi-GPU options:
- Horizontal tiling (split KV cache across GPUs with NVLink) is feasible but introduces latency overhead for KV gather on each token generation; it scales capacity but increases per-token latency by 10–30% depending on NVLink bandwidth and request size.
- Vertical sharding (model parallelism) reduces per-GPU memory for activations but complicates autoscaling and multi-tenant isolation.

PoC recommendation (practical):
- For a constrained PoC, aim for a 2x A100-80GB or equivalent NVLink pair per pod with NVSwitch where possible. With int8 KV packing we estimate a comfortable headroom margin (total ~120–160 GB across two GPUs after quantization overheads and system reservations).
- If you insist on single-GPU without tiling, move to an 80GB-class GPU plus aggressive KV eviction/prefetch for cold tails; expect lower session concurrency.

Next asks from our side:
- Can you share a sample token distribution (percentiles for request lengths and long-form windows)? A small sample (10–20 sessions) is fine.
- Any hard SLAs on latency (p50/p95) we need to guarantee during PoC?

I'm attaching a short spreadsheet with the numbers I used. We'll follow up with a more formal capacity plan after we see your telemetry.

Cheers,
Mina

Mina — helpful, thanks. Two clarifications and a small sample attached:

1) The model is actually a fine-tuned variant we call gino-7B-extended (same architecture, slightly wider kv layout). Your 1.1x KV multiplier still looks reasonable but we expect slightly higher memory pressure (~+8%).
2) Latency target: p50 < 150ms for small (<=256 token) generates, p95 < 450ms. If tiling adds >20% to p95 we need to pivot to single-GPU designs.

Attached: token_distribution_sample.json (example session traces). Can you convert these into the same bucket assumptions you used and re-run the sheet? If we can get two capacity scenarios (int8 pack and Q4x) with projected p95 latency impact, we can choose which variant to benchmark in the PoC.

Thanks — looping Dana on ops details.

Ari

1) Karthik: run two microbenchmarks this week — (a) int8-packed KV with NVLink tiling (2x80GB A100 with NVLink) and (b) Q4x with single 80GB GPU and aggressive KV eviction policy. Report p50/p95 and memory headroom. Use the attached token_distribution_sample.json as input.
2) Marcus: draft a one-pager for the customer clearly listing tradeoffs (expected p95 delta, operational complexity, fallback behavior) and recommend a default configuration for the PoC.
3) I'll prep a concise capacity plan and update the HubSpot deal (GNK-2027-058) with the two scenarios and cost delta.

Also note: make sure our telemetry hooks capture per-session KV hit rates and cross-GPU NVLink utilization during bench runs — those metrics will be critical for the post-PoC sizing conversation.
